newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight falls to 5.9/6.0 pct on bill maturity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight falls to 5.9/6.0 pct on bill maturity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 5.9/6.0 percent on Friday with the maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit which further improved market liquidity, dealers said.
It traded between six and 6.70 percent, after closing at 6.50/70 percent on Wednesday. The market was closed on Thursday for a religious holiday.
"The overnight is down because of the maturity. The overall market is thin as most players are staying away until the weekend," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

Dealers said with more funds coming into the market next week, the central bank was expected to call for a fresh bills or bonds issue soon. Rumours have been rife that Bank Negara will issue new long-term government bonds to roll over maturing bonds and help mop up excess liquidity.
A 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue will mature on May 15.
Earlier, interbank rates were steady with both borrowers and lenders largely sidelined.
One-week money was at 7.00/10 percent, two-week at 7.10/20 percent and three-week at 7.20/30 percent, all there or there abouts with Wednesday's levels.
One-month money was steady at 7.25/30 percent, three-month at 7.35/40 percent against 7.30/35 and six-month at 7.40/45 percent from 7.35/40.
Dealers said the market had been supported at the current levels, partly due to reduced activity.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were generally higher on expectations of softening of interest rates, futures market dealers said.
At 0800 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up one point to 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
September was up one to 92.69, or 7.31 percent.
March, June and September 1998 rose between four and seven.
